newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR CENTURY PUTS INDIA INTO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR CENTURY PUTS INDIA INTO FINAL.

text.p: Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar struck his 11th one-day century on Sunday as his side defeated Zimbabwe by six wickets to clinch a place in the final of the triangular tournament against hosts South Africa.
Tendulkar's hundred inspired the Indians to 241 for four off 39.2 overs to overhaul Zimbabwe's 240 for eight from 50 overs including 86 from their captain Alistair Campbell.
Starting the match with an inferior run rate to Zimbabwe, India needed to score their runs in 40.5 overs to reach Wednesday's final against South Africa in Durban.
Thanks to Tendulkar's century, and an unbeaten 56 from 66 balls from Ajay Jadeja, they got there with nine balls to spare and ousted Zimbabwe by 0.05 of a run on net run rate.
Tendulkar set out to dominate the bowling and after a sketchy start he demolished the Zimbabwean attack, eventually scoring 104 from 97 balls with a six and eight fours.
But when Tendulkar fell, caught by Campbell off the gentle seam bowling of Craig Evans, his side were still in trouble at 158 for four in the 28th over.
Zimbabwe should have settled the match shortly afterwards when Jadeja, on 19, lofted a catch into the deep but all-rounder Guy Whittall grassed the chance.
It was the key moment as Jadeja went on to hit 56 not out and share an unbroken partnership of 83 for the fifth wicket with Robin Singh who made 37 not out from 29 balls.

Earlier, Campbell had set the tone by top-scoring for Zimbabwe with 86 from 108 balls with two fours and two sixes. He added 61 for the second wicket with Grant Flower (40) and got good support in the middle order from Whittall (20) and Andy Flower (35).
But from 191 for three in the 41st over, the Zimbabweans lost their way against some tight bowling from Javagal Srinath, who took three for 35, and slow left-armer Sunil Joshi, three for 40.
India were also struggling 34 for two after the early dismissals of Saurav Ganguly and Mohammed Azharuddin, but Tendulkar's inspired innings settled the match in style.
